text:
I'll write the sketches directly: twelve scratch seeds, then seven ideas for the latent KV part, four of them leaps, two anchored on the gradient anomalies.

PASS 1 (scratch):
1. Break "a slot's key and value come from the same token": pair key s with value s+1 so one layer does induction. [kept, farthest]
2. Break "the latent depends only on its own token": 2-tap causal shift on the latent before the norm. [port, RWKV token shift]
3. Break "scores live in a per-head 64-d space": absorb the key expansion into the query, score against the 128-d latent directly.
4. Break "K and V are linear images of the latent": gated nonlinear expansion, since linearity only buys inference absorption we never use. [kept]
5. Break "a key carries no information about where it was seen": add the running mean of earlier latents to the key path. [kept]
6. Break "position gets 32 of 96 score dims": sweep the rope width. [tune]
7. Break "the rope slice is unnormalized while the content slice is normalized": norm qr and kr. [port]
8. Break "every layer compresses afresh": reuse the previous layer's latent. [needs Block, out of this part]
9. Break "all keys are per-token": append 16 chunk-mean latents as summary slots. [V4 HCA port, mask cost]
10. Break "the latent norm has one gain for both paths": separate key and value gains. [too small]
11. Break "values are the token's content": value is latent_s minus latent_{s-1}. [no mechanism for why loss drops]
12. Break "the latent is deterministic": noise on the latent. [no overfitting at 50M tokens, drop]
Existence operator: three mechanisms that could recover a third of the gap to a 2x model at ≤2% time are seeds 1, 3 and 4. At 45 matched steps each would have to show, respectively: recall-token loss already below baseline, matched-step loss below baseline at equal clip-norm, and matched-step loss below baseline with the gate not saturated.

IDEA: Successor-value heads
MECHANISM: Anomaly row restated: attention gradient in layer 2 is 15% below what layers 1 and 3 predict, the minimum of the depth profile. Three rivals: the detector flags the bottom of any U-shaped curve, an artifact of a three-point linear fit; the Sinkhorn mixing routed layer 2's output to a stream later layers read little, so its gradient is starved; layer 2 is the induction layer waiting for the prev-token circuit in layers 0-1 to form, so at step 100 its useful signal has not arrived. Five-minute probe on the step-100 checkpoint: measure for layers 1-3 the share of attention mass on offset -1 and on positions matching the current token's previous occurrence, plus the read weights later layers put on the stream layer 2 writes to. If the least popular rival holds, the fix is to let induction happen inside one layer: in three of six heads, query t attends to keys at s ≤ t-1 but retrieves the value built from latent_{s+1}, so "find my earlier occurrence, copy what followed" needs no two-layer composition and no prev-token head capacity.
PREDICTION: recall-token loss at step 100 from 4.475 to about 4.2 with other tokens unchanged; validation loss at 50M tokens lower by 0.02 to 0.04; zero extra parameters; step time within 2% since it is two SDPA calls on three heads each with shifted slices.
TEST: 100-step matched-seed run with the recall-token probe; if recall loss is not at least 0.1 below baseline at step 100 the mechanism is absent. A 3-step timing confirms the split SDPA cost.
SOURCE: own
TARGET: recall-token loss, down; secondary attention entropy in layers 2-4, down.
SCOPE: validation loss at 1024
KIND: leap
BREAKS: a key and the value it returns need not describe the same token; half the heads return the content of the token after the match.
KEEPS: same latent, same compress and expand matrices, same rope and norms, the other three heads unchanged, causality intact because s+1 ≤ t.
P_SUCCESS: 0.2
KILL: at 45 matched steps, recall-token loss not below baseline by 0.05, or total loss above baseline by 0.02.

IDEA: Latent token shift
MECHANISM: Anomaly row restated: attention gradient in layer 0 is ten times that of layers 1-11 on all three seeds. Three rivals: the layer-0 branch writes into a residual of RMS 1.4 versus 10.9 at the end, so the loss is most sensitive there; layer 0 is the only layer whose keys are built from raw token embeddings, so it alone carries the prev-token and bigram job that dominates early training; a measurement artifact, one micro-batch before clipping, where the compress and rotary matrices acting on near-one-hot normed embeddings inherit batch token composition and a 20-batch average would shrink the cell. Probe on the checkpoint: per-matrix gradient norms for wq, compress, expand, rotary and wo in layers 0-2 over 20 batches; rival one predicts uniform inflation across all five and the MLP too, rival two predicts concentration in compress and rotary, rival three predicts high variance and a smaller mean. If rival two holds, every layer should get cheap access to the previous token's content: mix the latent with the previous position's latent through a learned per-channel two-tap gate before the latent norm, so prev-token keys exist in every layer and layer 0 stops being a bottleneck.
PREDICTION: layer-0 attention gradient falls toward 0.1 as the job spreads; recall-token loss down 0.1 at step 100; validation loss lower by 0.01 to 0.02; 256 parameters per layer; step time unchanged within noise.
TEST: 1-minute smoke comparison at matched steps, plus the per-layer gradient table; if layer-0 grad norm does not drop by a third, the mechanism did not take over the job.
SOURCE: https://www.sebastianraschka.com/blog/2026/inkling-architecture-benchmark-notes.html (short causal convs on K and V), and RWKV token shift.
TARGET: gradient norm spread, down; recall-token loss, down.
SCOPE: validation loss at 1024
KIND: port

IDEA: Query scored against the latent
MECHANISM: The key expansion exists so that absorption is possible at inference; at 1024 context with no cache it is a cost paid for nothing, and it limits each head's score to rank 64 inside a 128-d latent. Drop the key expansion: keys are the normed latent itself, shared by all heads like multi-query attention, and each head's content query is a 128-d projection of the stream, normed per head. Muon then orthogonalizes one 384 by 960 query matrix instead of two chained matrices, and the score rank per head doubles.
PREDICTION: matched-step loss lower by 0.02 by step 500 and validation loss lower by 0.015 at 50M; parameters up 98,304 per layer, 1.18M total, within the cap; step time up about 3% from the 160-d score dot product.
TEST: build-only parameter count, 3-step timing, then a 100-step matched run; killed if matched-step loss is not below baseline at step 100.
SOURCE: own, building on the MLA absorption identity of DeepSeek-V2.
TARGET: attention entropy in deep layers, down; max attention logit unchanged because of the latent norm.
SCOPE: validation loss at 1024
KIND: leap
BREAKS: keys need not be per-head vectors in a 64-d space; all heads score directly against one shared 128-d latent.
KEEPS: compress, latent norm, value expansion, rope key, q-norm, wo, head count, causal mask.
P_SUCCESS: 0.18
KILL: at 45 matched steps, loss above baseline by 0.02 at equal gradient-clip ratio.

IDEA: Gated nonlinear expansion
MECHANISM: Linearity of expand is inherited from the inference recipe, but here the 128-d latent is a true bottleneck that six heads must share. Make the expansion a gated map, expand(c) times silu(gate(c)), so keys and values become a two-layer function of the latent and the six heads can carve different nonlinear views from the same 128 channels.
PREDICTION: validation loss lower by 0.01; parameters up 98,304 per layer, 1.18M total; step time up under 2%.
TEST: build-only count, 3-step timing, 100-step matched run; killed if the gate's mean activation stays near 0.5 and loss is not below baseline by step 100.
SOURCE: own
TARGET: validation loss only; secondary attention entropy in deep layers, down.
SCOPE: validation loss at 1024
KIND: leap
BREAKS: keys and values are a linear image of the latent.
KEEPS: compression, the norm, same latent width, same q path, same scores.
P_SUCCESS: 0.15
KILL: at 45 matched steps, loss not below baseline, or gate saturation above 90% of units.

IDEA: Prefix-conditioned keys
MECHANISM: A key describes only its own token, yet late positions lose 0.46 nats to early ones and the only context a key has is through the stream. Add to the key path the running mean of all earlier latents, computed once by cumulative sum in float32, scaled by a learned per-channel gate initialized near zero; values keep the pure latent. A query can then match "the word as used in this document's topic" rather than the bare word.
PREDICTION: late-minus-early loss gap shrinks from 0.46 by 0.05 at step 100; validation loss lower by 0.005 to 0.01; 128 parameters per layer; step time up under 1%.
TEST: 100-step matched run with the position-bucket probe; killed if positions 256-1024 are not below baseline while 0-64 are unchanged.
SOURCE: own
TARGET: loss at late positions, down.
SCOPE: validation loss at 1024
KIND: leap
BREAKS: a key is a function of its own token alone.
KEEPS: value path untouched, same expand, same norms and rope, causal mask.
P_SUCCESS: 0.12
KILL: at 45 matched steps, the late-position bucket is not below baseline by 0.03.

IDEA: Rope width sweep
MECHANISM: Position holds 32 of the 96 score dimensions with a single unnormalized shared rope key, a split copied from V4 and never tested at this width. Changing rd rebalances how much of the logit budget is positional versus content.
PREDICTION: at rd 16, parameters down 43k per layer and late-position loss up; at rd 48 or 64, parameters up 65k or 86k per layer and late-position loss down by 0.02 to 0.05 at step 100; validation effect in the range of 0.01 either way.
TEST: sweep rd in {16, 48, 64}, 100 matched steps each with the position-bucket probe.
SOURCE: own
TARGET: loss at late positions.
SCOPE: validation loss at 1024
KIND: tune

IDEA: Normalized rope slice
MECHANISM: qr and kr are the only unnormalized pieces of the score, so the maximum logit of 22.75 at layer 8 can come from them growing without a bound while the content slice is pinned by q-norm and k-norm. RMS-normalize qr per head and kr once, with learned gains, so the whole dot product has a controlled scale and the positional term cannot drown the content term.
PREDICTION: max attention logit at layer 8 falls below 16; validation loss lower by 0.005; 64 parameters per layer; no measurable time cost.
TEST: 100-step matched run with the max-logit probe; killed if logits do not fall or loss rises.
SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.02770 (Gemma 4 QKNorm), extended to the rope slice.
TARGET: max attention logit, down.
SCOPE: validation loss at 1024
KIND: port

Recap: seven sketches, four leaps, two anchored on the layer-0 and layer-2 gradient anomalies. The strongest first test is successor-value heads, since it costs no parameters and its kill signal, recall-token loss at 45 steps, is cheap to read.
